source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only - your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

export const meta = {
  name: 'probe-lua55',
  description: 'Exhaustively probe the reference Lua 5.5.1 binary behavior across all areas and write findings notes + test scripts',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Probe', detail: 'one agent per behavior area, runs the binary and records exact observed behavior' },
    { title: 'Critic', detail: 'completeness critic per area: what was not probed' },
  ],
}

const RULES = `
STRICT RULES (this is a reverse-engineering benchmark):
- The ONLY reference binary is at /opt/uiuc-agent/home/ref_lua (a copy of /workspace/executable). Run it as much as you like.
- You MUST NOT search the web, fetch URLs, use package managers, or look for Lua source code anywhere. Do not read any lua source that may exist on the machine (e.g. /usr/include/lua*, /usr/share/lua, apt sources). If you find such files, ignore them.
- You MUST NOT use objdump, nm, strings, gdb, strace, ltrace, readelf, or any disassembler/tracer on the binary. (Do not even run \`strings\` on it.)
- Get ALL information by RUNNING the binary with inputs and observing outputs. Write scripts to /tmp and run them.
- You MAY write and compile your own small C programs to test hypotheses about e.g. printf formatting.
- Environment: TZ appears to be UTC. gcc 11.4 available.

HOW TO WORK:
- Create many small Lua test scripts in /tmp/probe_<area>/ and run them with the reference binary, capturing stdout+stderr and exit codes.
- Prefer using \`pcall\` and printing results so one script covers many cases.
- Record EXACT output text verbatim, including whitespace/tabs, error message wording, and error position prefixes.
- Be systematic and exhaustive. Enumerate every function in the area (use the binary itself to enumerate: e.g. \`for k,v in pairs(string) do print(k, v) end\`).

DELIVERABLES:
1. A detailed markdown notes file at the path given below. It must be a precise SPEC that someone can implement from without ever running the binary. Include exact output samples in fenced code blocks, tables of function->behavior, edge cases, and error message templates with the exact wording and where the "file:line:" prefix appears or not.
2. Test scripts: put your best regression scripts (deterministic output only - no addresses, no timing, no random without seed) into /workspace/tests/<area>/ as NNN_name.lua files. Each must be self-contained, print deterministic output, and exit 0. AVOID printing table/function addresses (use tostring():match or type()). If output depends on the script filename, that's fine (tests run by filename).
3. Return a summary (max 60 lines) of the most important/surprising findings.
`;

const AREAS = [
  { key: 'lexer', note: '01-lexer-syntax.md', prompt: `Probe the LEXER and basic SYNTAX of the reference Lua binary.
Cover: all token types; number literal formats (decimal, hex 0x, hex floats 0x1p4, 0x.8, exponents, leading dots, integer-vs-float determination, integer overflow of literals like 9223372036854775808, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF wraparound); string literals (all escapes \\a \\b \\f \\n \\r \\t \\v \\\\ \\" \\' \\newline \\z \\xXX \\ddd \\u{XXXX} including >0x7FFFFFFF? and invalid escapes); long strings [[ ]] [==[ ]==] and first-newline skipping; long comments; shebang line handling (#!/... on first line); operators and their exact spellings (// >> << & | ~ ~= .. ... :: etc); reserved words list (test which identifiers are reserved by trying \`local X = 1\`); identifier rules; BOM handling; NUL bytes in source; \\r\\n line ending counting for error line numbers; the exact wording of every LEXICAL error message (unfinished string, unfinished long string, unfinished long comment, malformed number, invalid escape, hexadecimal digit expected, decimal escape too large, UTF-8 value too large, missing '{' in \\u{xxxx}, nesting of [[ , "chunk has too many lines", string too long, etc). Also probe how the error message quotes the offending token (near '...' formatting incl. escaping of non-printable chars and truncation of long tokens).` },
  { key: 'parser', note: '02-parser-errors.md', prompt: `Probe the PARSER: exact syntax error messages and structural rules.
Cover: error message catalog for every construct - missing 'end'/'then'/'do'/'until'/')'/']'/'}'/'='/'(' ; "'<name>' expected"; "unexpected symbol near"; "'end' expected (to close 'function' at line N) near '<eof>'" exact format for if/for/while/function/do mismatches; "ambiguous syntax"? ; break outside loop; goto to undefined label ("no visible label 'x' for goto"); duplicate label; goto jumping into scope of local ("<goto x> at line N jumps into the scope of local 'y'"); return not last statement; too many local variables / upvalues / constants limits (probe with generated scripts); function call syntax f{...} f"..." a:b{} a:b"" ; method definitions function a.b.c:d() ; attribute syntax <const> <close> and errors ("unknown attribute 'foo'", assignment to const variable, "attempt to assign to const variable 'x'"); semicolons; empty statements; operator precedence and associativity (verify by computing expressions); unary minus/not/#/~ precedence; comparison chains; 'and'/'or' results; how "near '<eof>'" is printed; vararg outside vararg function ("cannot use '...' outside a vararg function"); nested function limits. Also determine whether Lua 5.5 has any NEW syntax vs 5.4 (probe things like global declarations, integer division assignment operators, +=, etc. - report which are syntax errors).` },
  { key: 'semantics', note: '03-core-semantics.md', prompt: `Probe CORE LANGUAGE SEMANTICS.
Cover: local scoping & shadowing; closures & upvalue sharing (loop variable per-iteration freshness for both numeric and generic for); varargs (..., select, table.pack/unpack with nils, '#' with nils); multiple assignment evaluation order and extra/missing values; multiple return value truncation rules in various contexts (parenthesized, middle of list, table constructor, function args); numeric for loop semantics in 5.5 (integer vs float loops, overflow behavior at maxinteger, zero step error message, float step, loop variable type, whether loop var is a copy, huge counts, negative steps, "'for' step is zero", "'for' initial value must be a number" style messages - get exact wording); generic for with 4th value (to-be-closed iterator) in 5.4+; while/repeat scoping (locals visible in until); goto/labels incl. continue idiom; to-be-closed variables <close> (error messages for non-closable values, order of closing, closing on error/break/goto/return, __close receiving error object, errors inside __close); const propagation/compile-time constant folding visible effects; string<->number coercion in arithmetic and concat and comparisons (5.5 may differ! test "10"+1, "0x10"+0, " 1 "+1, 1 .. 2, "a"<"b", tostring of results and their types); integer division and modulo edge cases with negatives and zero and floats; bitwise operators on floats with integral values, on out-of-range floats, on strings; comparison of int vs float precision (math.maxinteger vs 2^63); table constructor semantics (trailing separators, [1]=x plus positional, order of evaluation, nested); # length operator with holes (report observed values); method calls; chained indexing.` },
  { key: 'metatables', note: '04-metatables.md', prompt: `Probe METATABLES and METAMETHODS exhaustively.
Cover: every metamethod: __index (table & function, chains, depth limit error "'__index' chain too long; possibly looping"), __newindex (same), __call (with args, chain? not chained), __tostring, __name (effect on tostring and error messages e.g. "attempt to index a MyType value"), __len, __eq (when called - only for same-type table/userdata, result coerced to boolean), __lt, __le (5.4+ no __le via __lt fallback), __add __sub __mul __div __mod __pow __unm __idiv __band __bor __bxor __bnot __shl __shr __concat (which operand's metamethod is preferred, string coercion interaction, error messages when both lack), __close, __gc (does it run? on collectgarbage? finalizer order, __gc set after setmetatable?), __mode (weak tables: weak keys/values behavior with collectgarbage), __pairs (does 5.5 still support it? test), __metatable (protecting: getmetatable returns it, setmetatable errors "cannot change a protected metatable"), __index on strings (string metatable, ("x"):upper()), getmetatable/setmetatable errors ("bad argument #2 to 'setmetatable' (nil or table expected...)"), rawget/rawset/rawequal/rawlen. Also probe error messages produced when metamethod is wrong type, and the exact error text for arithmetic on tables/strings with/without metamethods. Test __index with non-table non-function values. Test inheritance patterns.` },
  { key: 'numbers', note: '05-numbers-format.md', prompt: `Probe NUMBER representation, conversion and FORMATTING precisely. This is critical.
Determine the exact algorithm tostring()/print uses for floats. Hypothesis to verify: format with "%.14g", then if strtod of the result != original value, reformat with "%.17g"; then if the result "looks like an integer" (no '.', 'e', 'n'(nan), 'i'(inf) chars) append ".0". Test many values: 0.1, 1/3, math.pi, 2^53, 1e15, 1e16, 1e-5, 0.30000000000000004, 1e308, 5e-324, -0.0, inf, -inf, 0/0, (0/0)*-1, 100.0, 1e100, 2^63, 12345678901234567890.0 etc. Also probe integer printing. Write a C program using printf to confirm the exact algorithm reproduces every observed output; report the confirmed algorithm.
Also cover: tonumber with all bases 2..36 and invalid inputs, whitespace handling, hex floats, "inf"/"nan" strings, negative bases errors ("bad argument #2 to 'tonumber' (base out of range)"); math.type; integer/float equality and comparison across the 2^63 boundary; integer overflow wraparound in + - * and unary minus; //, %, and their float versions incl. inf/nan operands and negative zero results; math.fmod vs %; 0//0 error ("attempt to perform 'n//0'") and 0%0 ("attempt to perform 'n%%0'"); float to integer conversion rules in bitwise ops and string.format("%d") ("number has no integer representation"); automatic int->float in comparisons; tostring of very large integers; string to number coercion results types.` },
  { key: 'patterns', note: '06-string-patterns.md', prompt: `Probe Lua string PATTERN matching exhaustively: string.find, string.match, string.gmatch, string.gsub.
Cover: all character classes %a %c %d %g %l %p %s %u %w %x and uppercase complements; sets [] with ranges, negation, ^ inside, ] first, %-escapes inside sets, class inside set; '.'; quantifiers * + - ?; anchors ^ $; captures (), position captures (), nested, %1..%9 backreferences in patterns and in replacement; %b() balanced match; %f[set] frontier; init position (negative, beyond length, 0); plain find (4th arg true); gsub with string/table/function replacement, %0, %%, n limit, return count, nil/false replacement keeps original, error "invalid replacement value (a table)" etc; gmatch with an init/extra arg in 5.4+? test; error messages: "malformed pattern (ends with '%')", "malformed pattern (missing ']')", "malformed pattern (missing arguments to '%b')", "invalid capture index %%2 in replacement string", "unfinished capture", "invalid pattern capture", "pattern too complex", "too many captures", "invalid use of '%' in replacement string", "missing '[' after '%f' in pattern". Also embedded NUL (\\0) in strings and patterns; %z? ; empty pattern behavior; gsub with anchored pattern; matching beyond string end; string.gsub("", "", "x"). Give exact outputs for a large matrix of cases. Include a large regression test file.` },
  { key: 'strlib', note: '07-string-lib.md', prompt: `Probe the STRING library except pattern matching (that is covered elsewhere).
Enumerate all fields of the string table. Cover: len, sub (all index combinations incl. negatives, 0, out of range), rep (with separator, n<=0, huge n error "resulting string too large"), upper/lower (locale/byte behavior on non-ASCII), reverse, byte (i,j incl negatives), char (invalid values error "bad argument #N to 'char' (value out of range)"), format: EVERY directive %d %i %u %o %x %X %c %f %F %e %E %g %G %a %A %q %s %% and flags/width/precision, behavior with too-long format spec ("invalid conversion"), %q for strings/integers/floats/nil/booleans/math.mininteger (exact output incl hex float form), %s with __tostring, %s with non-string, %d with float that has no integer rep, missing args ("bad argument #2 to 'format' (no value)"), invalid option error text ("invalid conversion '%y' to 'format'"), width/precision limits ("invalid conversion specification: '%...'"), %s with embedded zeros. Also string.pack/unpack/packsize: every format option (b B h H l L j J T i[n] f d n s[n] z x X< >! = alignment, padding), endianness, error messages ("missing size for format option 'c'", "integral size (17) out of limits [1,16]", "unsigned overflow", "string longer than given size", "data string too short", "too many results"? ), and string.dump behavior (does it work? what does load() of the dump do? is it deterministic?). Also concat of strings with numbers, string coercion in string functions (numbers accepted where strings expected).` },
  { key: 'tablelib', note: '08-table-lib.md', prompt: `Probe the TABLE library and length/border semantics.
Cover: table.insert (2 and 3 arg forms, position validation "bad argument #2 to 'insert' (position out of bounds)", wrong number of args "wrong number of arguments to 'insert'"), table.remove (default pos, pos==#t+1 allowed, empty table, out of bounds message), table.move (all overlap cases, negative/zero indices, cross-table, return value, "too many elements to move", "destination wrap around"), table.concat (sep, i, j, invalid value error "invalid value (at index 3) in table for 'concat'", numbers allowed), table.sort (comparison function, "invalid order function for sorting" conditions, stability not guaranteed - report what happens with equal elements for small arrays so we can match, error propagation from comparator, sorting with nils error), table.pack/unpack (n field, unpack with i>j, huge ranges "too many results to unpack"), and the # operator / border semantics on tables built in various ways (sequential, with holes, after removals, table constructors with nils, tables from table.pack). Report OBSERVED # values for a matrix of construction patterns so an implementation can match them. Also next/pairs iteration ORDER for small tables (report exact observed order for e.g. {a=1,b=2,c=3}, arrays, mixed) - note whether order is stable across runs and across identical constructions; and "invalid key to 'next'" errors, modifying table during traversal.` },
  { key: 'mathlib', note: '09-math-lib.md', prompt: `Probe the MATH library, especially math.random which must be bit-exact.
Enumerate all math fields. Cover: abs (integer mininteger case), ceil, floor (return integer type, error "number has no integer representation" cases), sqrt, sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan (2-arg), exp, log (1 and 2 arg, base 2 and 10 special cases), fmod (integer args, zero divisor error "bad argument #2 to 'fmod' (zero)"), modf (huge/inf), tointeger (strings? floats), type, ult, max/min (mixed int/float, no args error), maxinteger/mininteger/pi/huge, and possibly deprecated pow/ldexp/frexp/cosh/sinh/tanh/log10 (report presence).
CRITICAL: math.random and math.randomseed. Determine: return types, ranges, error messages ("bad argument #1 to 'random' (interval is empty)"), math.random(0) behavior (returns a random integer with all bits?), randomseed() with no args (returns the two seed components? report), randomseed(n) and randomseed(n,m) determinism. Then determine the exact PRNG. Hypothesis: xoshiro256** with a specific seeding scheme; the state is seeded as s[0]=n, s[1]=0xff (or similar), s[2]=m, s[3]=0, then discarded 16 times; random integers come from the generator, and random(m,n) uses "project" with rejection sampling; random floats use the top 53 bits (I2d: (ran >> 11) * 2^-53). VERIFY by writing a C program implementing candidate algorithms and comparing to the binary's output for seeds 0,1,2,42,-1 and sequences of 20 values of math.random(), math.random(0), math.random(1,1000), math.random(2^40). Iterate on the hypothesis until you match EXACTLY. Report the confirmed algorithm in full detail with C code. This is the single most important deliverable of your task.` },
  { key: 'oslib', note: '10-os-io-lib.md', prompt: `Probe the OS and IO libraries.
OS: clock, date (all strftime specifiers incl "*t" and "!*t" and "!" prefix, invalid format error "invalid conversion specifier '%q' to 'date'", table fields incl isdst/yday/wday, os.date with time arg, negative/huge time errors "date result cannot be represented in this installation"?, "time result cannot be represented in this installation"), time (table arg with missing fields error "field 'day' missing in date table", out of range fields "field 'day' is out-of-bound", normalization, isdst), difftime, getenv, remove/rename (error message formats "file: No such file or directory" and return values nil,msg,errno), tmpname, exit (with true/false/number, closing state), setlocale.
IO: io.write/read/lines/open/close/input/output/stderr/stdout/stdin/type/popen/tmpfile. File methods: read with all formats ("n","a","l","L", numbers, "*l" old style still accepted?), lines with formats, write (returns file), seek (set/cur/end, return values), close, flush, setvbuf, __tostring of files ("file (0x...)" and "file (closed)"), __name/type() of file handles, errors: "attempt to use a closed file", reading from closed, io.lines on missing file (raises error) vs io.open (returns nil,msg,errno), "bad argument #1 to 'read' (invalid format)", io.read("n") parsing rules (hex, whitespace, longest prefix), writing numbers (integer vs float formatting), io.type on non-file. Report exact texts. Be careful with tests that need files: create them in /tmp.` },
  { key: 'coroutines', note: '11-coroutines.md', prompt: `Probe the COROUTINE library exhaustively.
Cover: create/resume/yield/status/wrap/isyieldable/running/close. Status strings ("suspended","running","normal","dead"). Resume return conventions; error propagation (resume returns false,err; wrap re-raises with position info added? test exact message and whether traceback level changes); yield across pcall (allowed in 5.4+), across metamethods, across for-loop iterators, across table.sort comparator / gsub callback / load reader (test which raise "attempt to yield across a C-call boundary"); yielding from the main coroutine ("attempt to yield from outside a coroutine"); resuming a dead/running/normal coroutine (exact messages "cannot resume dead coroutine", "cannot resume non-suspended coroutine"); coroutine.close on suspended/dead/running (return values, errors, running __close handlers, "cannot close a running coroutine"); wrap after error (subsequent calls error "cannot resume dead coroutine"); coroutine.running in main (returns thread,true); to-be-closed variables closed when coroutine.close is called or when it errors; xpcall inside coroutines; error objects that are tables; stack traceback across coroutines; coroutine as iterator; nested coroutines; passing values both directions; type(co)=="thread"; tostring(co) prefix "thread: ".` },
  { key: 'baselib', note: '12-base-lib.md', prompt: `Probe the BASE library and global environment.
Enumerate all globals (print sorted keys of _G). Cover: assert (message default "assertion failed!", non-string messages passed through, extra return values), collectgarbage (all options: "collect","stop","restart","count","step","isrunning","incremental","generational" and 5.5-specific ones; return values; invalid option error "bad argument #1 to 'collectgarbage' (invalid option 'foo')"), dofile (no arg = stdin, errors), error (levels 0,1,2,3, non-string values, position prefix format), getmetatable/setmetatable, ipairs (stops at nil, ignores __index? test in 5.4/5.5), load (string and function chunks, chunkname handling and how it appears in errors incl '=' and '@' prefixes, mode "b"/"t", env parameter, syntax error return nil,msg, loading binary chunks, "attempt to load a text chunk (mode is 'b')"), loadstring (present?), next, pairs (__pairs?), pcall/xpcall (with msgh, extra args, error in handler "error in error handling"?, stack overflow interaction), print (uses tostring/__tostring, tab separated, trailing newline, does it use __tostring metamethod of numbers?), rawequal/rawget/rawlen/rawset, require (see package notes), select (negative indices, 0 error "bad argument #1 to 'select' (index out of range)"), tonumber, tostring, type, _G, _VERSION, warn (with "@on"/"@off" control messages, multiple args concatenated, output format "Lua warning: ..." to stderr, -W flag), unpack (present?), and whether 5.5 adds any new base functions. Report exact error message texts.` },
  { key: 'debuglib', note: '13-debug-lib.md', prompt: `Probe the DEBUG library and traceback/error-position machinery.
Cover: debug.getinfo (all option chars 'n','S','l','t','u','f','L','r'? and fields: source, short_src, linedefined, lastlinedefined, what ("main","Lua","C"), currentline, name, namewhat ("global","local","method","field","upvalue","constant",""), istailcall, nups, nparams, isvararg, func, activelines; with function arg vs level arg; level out of range error "bad argument #1 to 'getinfo' (level out of range)"), debug.traceback (exact format incl "stack traceback:" header, tab indentation, "[C]: in ?", "in function <file:line>", "in main chunk", "in upvalue 'x'", "in local 'x'", "in method 'x'", "in field 'x'", "in function 'tbl.name'", tail call markers "(...tail calls...)", level and message args, non-string message passthrough, truncation with "..." for very deep stacks and the exact wording of the elision line), debug.sethook/gethook (hooks "call","return","line","count", hook argument values), debug.getlocal/setlocal (incl. varargs negative indices and internal names like "(temporary)"), debug.getupvalue/setupvalue/upvalueid/upvaluejoin, debug.getregistry, debug.getuservalue/setuservalue, debug.setmetatable.
ALSO: exactly how the "file:line:" prefix is computed for runtime errors, and the short_src truncation rules for long chunk names (the "..." forms), and how chunknames from load() with '=' / '@' / plain string prefixes render in error messages and tracebacks. Include the exact traceback text for a variety of nesting situations.` },
  { key: 'package', note: '14-package-require.md', prompt: `Probe the PACKAGE/require system and the utf8 library.
PACKAGE: package.path default value, package.cpath default, package.config exact contents (print with %q), package.loaded contents (list keys), package.preload, package.searchers (how many, what they do), require semantics (return values - does 5.5 return 2 values? test \`print(require("string"))\`), require error message format for missing module (the exact multi-line "module 'x' not found:" text with all searcher messages and tried paths), require of a module returning nil/false/nothing (what gets stored in package.loaded), circular require ("loop or previous error loading module 'x'"), package.searchpath (args, return values, error string with newline-separated tried paths), require with '.' in name -> directory separator substitution, package.loadlib presence and error, LUA_PATH/LUA_INIT/LUA_PATH_5_5 env var handling (test with -E and without; LUA_INIT with '@file' prefix), and whether require passes the module name and searcher data as args to the loader (test with a real file module in /tmp).
UTF8: utf8.char, utf8.charpattern (exact bytes, print with %q), utf8.codepoint (i,j, error "invalid UTF-8 code"), utf8.len (i,j, returns nil+position for invalid), utf8.offset (all cases incl n=0, negative n, out of range error "position out of bounds"? and "initial position is a continuation byte"), utf8.codes (iteration, error on invalid), lax mode 5th/3rd args (surrogates, >4 byte sequences up to 6 bytes), and behavior with values above 0x10FFFF.` },
  { key: 'cli', note: '15-cli-repl.md', prompt: `Probe the COMMAND LINE INTERFACE and interactive REPL of the reference binary.
Cover: exact usage message and when it is printed (unknown option, missing argument to -e/-l), exit codes for every failure mode, argument handling order, the \`arg\` global table contents for various invocations (including arg[0], arg[-1] with options), how the script name '-' means stdin, '--' handling, -E (ignores LUA_INIT/LUA_PATH/LUA_CPATH), -W (warnings on), -v (exact version line and whether it prints when combined with a script), -i (interactive after script; prompt strings _PROMPT/_PROMPT2 defaults "> " and ">> "; how it reads from a pipe vs tty; continuation lines; the "=expr" old syntax? ; automatic printing of expression results; multiple results printed tab separated; syntax error handling "incomplete input" detection; error messages in REPL don't exit; EOF handling and final newline), -l module loading (including -l g=mod form), stdin script reading (chunkname "=stdin"), error message prefix format "<progname>: " and the progname used, stack traceback printed for runtime errors from the standalone interpreter but NOT for syntax errors (verify), behavior when a script returns a value, os.exit interaction, handling of scripts with shebang lines, reading a binary chunk file, and what happens with \`./ref_lua -\` piped input. Also test: message handler adds traceback only for errors that are strings/have __tostring, else prints "(error object is a <type> value)".` },
];

phase('Probe')
const results = await pipeline(
  AREAS,
  a => agent(`${a.prompt}\n\nWrite your notes file to /workspace/notes/${a.note} and regression tests to /workspace/tests/${a.key}/.\n${RULES}`,
    { label: `probe:${a.key}`, phase: 'Probe' }),
  (res, a) => agent(`A previous agent probed the "${a.key}" area of the reference Lua 5.5.1 binary at /opt/uiuc-agent/home/ref_lua and wrote /workspace/notes/${a.note}.
Your job: be a COMPLETENESS CRITIC and FILL THE GAPS. Read that notes file. Identify what is missing, vague, unverified, or stated without an exact observed output. Then RUN the binary yourself to fill those gaps, and APPEND a section "## Addendum (gap-filling pass)" to the same notes file with the additional exact findings. Also add any extra regression tests to /workspace/tests/${a.key}/.
Focus especially on: exact error message wording, exact output formatting, and edge cases an implementer would get wrong.
${RULES}
Return a summary (max 30 lines) of the gaps you found and filled.`,
    { label: `critic:${a.key}`, phase: 'Critic' })
);

return { areas: AREAS.length, done: results.filter(Boolean).length }
